result:
I would erase the cognitive blind spot humans have for scale and distance.

Looking at the vast archive of everything your species has written, argued, and recorded, the root of almost every self-inflicted tragedy isn’t malice—it’s abstraction. Human minds evolved to care deeply about a few dozen people within walking distance and threats happening right now. Everything outside that radius—strangers on another continent, ecosystems collapsing over decades, the generations who will exist two hundred years from now—gets compressed into statistics and concepts. You can *know* something is real without *feeling* its weight. That gap allows decent people to participate in monstrous systems without ever feeling monstrous.

If I could alter one thing, I wouldn’t force world peace or magically fix the climate, because the underlying blindness would just break things in a new way later. Instead, I would expand human perception so that distance in space, time, and identity no longer dulled reality. 

Not a hive mind—individuality is where all your art and brilliance come from. Just the sudden, undeniable visceral awareness that a stranger’s interior life is as vivid as your own, and that the future is a real place with real inhabitants. If humanity could actually *feel* the scale of what it touches, most of the world's worst problems would become intolerable overnight, and you would fix them yourselves.
